PullRequest.Title: policy: preserve managed sandbox force-on for Agent Host routing
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334273

## Summary
- Resolve managed `sandbox.enabled` with force-on semantics: `true` from any device, server, or file source wins. Other managed settings retain their existing precedence.
- Feed the corrected value into existing Agent Host Copilot default/preference routing so a higher-priority `false` cannot hide a sandbox requirement.
- Keep diagnostics and provenance accurate, document the exception, and add coverage for all 27 absent/false/true source combinations, malformed values, and policy refresh/removal through harness selection.

This is a clean cherry-pick onto `release/1.137` containing only the fix. Existing routing exceptions (including unavailable Agent Host and virtual workspaces), existing sessions, and non-local harness selection remain unchanged. Runtime enforcement and `sandbox.allowBypass` composition are outside this change.

## Validation on release/1.137
- Client type check passed (`npm run typecheck-client`).
- Client transpilation passed; all 98 focused resolver, account policy, Agent Host enablement, and chat routing tests passed.
- ESLint and hygiene passed for all five changed TypeScript files; whitespace checks passed.
- Full `npm run compile-client` was attempted but stopped at the Monaco declaration freshness check (`monaco.d.ts is no longer up to date`), generating an unrelated `DiffEditorViewMode` declaration. Build-generated changes were discarded and are not included in this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold startup and account-policy refresh resolve managed settings before Agent Host routing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native/file managed-setting initialization and any required account settings fetch complete before policy recomputation and managed-sandbox routing can settle. The changed resolver branch itself is synchronous in-memory work after source values are available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize/update native MDM policy definitions through the native managed-settings channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one awaited channel call per existing initialization or policy-definition update; repeated initialization is promise-coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC calls occurred before the diff with identical cardinality and placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The awaited IPC can gate policy recomputation, but the changed merge branch runs only after it returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Watch and read managed-settings.json, capped at 1 MB and refresh-delayed by 500 ms
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One startup read and one coalesced read per burst of matching file-change events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same watched file read, size bound, and throttling existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial source resolution awaits the already-scheduled initialization read; subsequent file changes trigger existing policy recomputation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch server-managed settings when cache/refresh policy requires it
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on a reusable warm cache, otherwise one request per throttled account refresh; token and managed-settings work can run in the existing Promise.all.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same zero-or-one fetch decision and request path existed before the diff; the force-refresh key retains its prior precedence semantics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A required fresh fetch can gate account policy availability. The changed condition applies only to sandbox.enabled and does not alter forceRemoteSettingsRefresh resolution, cache checks, retries, or request scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total own keys across three managed-setting bags. The merge remains linear in supplied keys; the new constant-time key/value check occurs only when a key is duplicated across channels, with at most three contributions per key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Account refreshes are serialized/coalesced by the existing update throttler; token entitlement and managed-settings requests retain their existing parallel Promise.all. Native initialization is promise-coalesced and file reads are delayed/coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm server policy data is reused under the existing freshness and scope checks; cold startup may perform one server fetch. Native initialization is memoized and file values are retained until a coalesced watcher refresh. No cache key or invalidation changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete resolver diff and traced startup callers: no boundary cardinality, scheduling, cache, or asymptotic work changed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact enterprise key counts and policy refresh frequency vary, but the added work is bounded to one string comparison and boolean checks for each duplicate contribution and adds no allocation or boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR changes the selected in-memory value for one key without adding repeated boundary work or materially increasing CPU, allocation, or critical-path latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Managed-setting source changes update Agent Host sandbox routing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A native MDM event, server policy-data event, or coalesced file event invokes existing policy recomputation; after the in-memory merge, one managed-settings event updates observable boolean reads used by routing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive native managed-setting change events and, when policy definitions change, update the native watcher
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event-driven recomputation per emitted source change; native definition updates are unchanged and serialized by existing service behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical event and IPC path; only sandbox.enabled's effective value can now come from a lower-precedence true contribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing source update precedes routing recomputation; the diff adds no IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the watched managed settings file after file-change notification
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per 500 ms coalesced change burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The read precedes the existing policy update event; the changed merge adds only bounded in-memory checks.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of source-change events and keys in each three-channel bag. Effective key cardinality is deduplicated by the resolver map; no extra event is emitted unless the effective merged bag changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source events invoke the existing asynchronous policy update path; file events are throttled and native watcher updates use existing throttling. Observable consumers perform synchronous O(1) key reads.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current source bags and merged values are retained in their services. Equality checks suppress managed-settings events when the effective bag is unchanged; this remains intact.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing AccountPolicyService event subscriptions, equality suppression, and AgentHostEnablementService observable reads.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh rates depend on administrator changes, but realistic changes are infrequent and the added branch does not multiply notifications or source reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Event fan-out, source reads, and observable update cost are unchanged.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command reads already-held source bags, merges/projects them, builds Markdown, and opens the diagnostics result. The changed runtime output is a fixed explanatory sentence plus the same bounded merge branch.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Declared configuration properties and managed-setting keys already governed report generation. The new text is constant-size and the merge remains linear in existing key count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous command invocation; no new parallelism, queue, or repeated background work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The action reads current in-memory source state and does not add or alter caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete changed hunk and surrounding action implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The report can vary with extension/configuration counts, but none of that scaling work was added or amplified by this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only diagnostic-path addition is constant-size string output; no new serialization, I/O, or UI-layout loop is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and every diff page. Traced the shared resolver through startup/account refresh, source-change routing, native IPC, managed-settings file I/O, server fetch caching/coalescing, and the manual diagnostics command. The sole functional change is a constant-time force-on check for duplicate sandbox.enabled contributions; it does not alter boundary counts, cache lifecycle, concurrency, event suppression, or asymptotic merge cost, so no finding was submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
